description:
Built-in tool that retrieves the result of an in-flight dispatch (ARCH §2.5). The other half of the dispatch/await pair.

Wire shape:
- Tool name: await
- Input schema: { handle: string (required) }. The handle is a sub-conv-id (i.e. a branch name).
- Skill: <harness-root>/skills/await/SKILL.md.
- Stdout (tool_result.content): JSON object. On successful subagent merge: {status: 'merged', summary: '<terminal-summary text>'}. The summary is the contents of summary/<NNN>.md from the subagent's terminal compactor (already produced in v0.3 via the existing compactor primitive). On stop: {status: 'stopped'}. On conflict: {status: 'conflicted'} (§2.6 step 6 — harness defect surface).
- Exit 0 in all three terminal cases (the in-band status field communicates outcome to the agent — same pattern as adapter's in-band errors §4.4).

Behavior:
- Blocks the calling tool until the named subagent reaches a terminal state. Implementation: poll git refs / merge state. Per §2.5 every tool returns synchronously; await is no exception, it just returns synchronously after a wait.
- Terminal detection: subagent branch is merged into its parent (status=merged), has the stopped marker in its state dir (status=stopped), or is flagged conflicted by the merge protocol (status=conflicted).
- Tool-call commit on parent branch per §3.3: input.json + output.json under steps/<parent-conv-id>/<NNN>/tools/<tool-id>/.

Out of scope:
- check(handle) (non-blocking poll). Filed as a v0.5+ follow-on if needed.
- Timeout knobs. Default behavior: block forever or until the harness terminates.
- Workflow.yaml-driven 'on subagent termination' actions. v0.6.

Tests:
- Happy path: dispatch a subagent (with a stub harness that writes a summary and merges back), await, get {status: merged, summary: '...'}.
- Stop path: dispatch a subagent that gets stopped, await, get {status: stopped}.
- Conflict path: simulate a conflicted merge, await, get {status: conflicted}.
- Single-source-of-truth: no sidecar handle index — every state read is via git.

Done-when: a step that emits tool_use {name: await, input: {handle: '<sub-conv-id>'}} produces a per-call commit on the parent branch, blocks until the subagent terminates, and returns the appropriate status object as tool_result.content.
title: v0.4 Phase 3: built-in tool — await
